findings.title: Crate example still accesses private recovered-result fields
findings.reproduction: Run cargo test --locked --release -j 2 -- --test-threads=2. The crate-level no_run example still calls assert_eq!(*phrase.phrase, original); after RecoveredPhrase fields became private. The API example comment also describes direct .words/.verified/.phrase/.suite fields.
findings.expected: All supported examples compile against the current accessors, and the ordinary cargo test gate succeeds without a filtered doctest subset.
findings.observed: Library 301/CLI 105 tests pass, plus 3 suite-3 and 2 suite-4 nonignored tests. Doctests: 3 passed, 1 failed; E0616 private phrase field; overall exit 101. Warning-denied cargo doc passes, which does not compile no_run examples.
findings.impact: Limited documentation adaptation defect; no runtime encryption failure. It blocks the mandatory ordinary cargo-test/check.sh/CI gate and therefore release readiness, independently of Low severity.
findings.recommendedFix: Use phrase.phrase() without dereferencing a private field; update the API example comment to words(), verified(), phrase() and suite().
findings.requiredVerification: Run the entire cargo test --locked --doc suite and the normal native test/check gate, not only the two newly added ownership doctests.

findings.title: Drawing rejects invalid first UTF-8 before guarding its repeat allocation
findings.reproduction: Run the retained draw-utf8.mjs against the recorded dist. Direct draw binding: invalid first UTF-8 with a synthetic marker repetition. Public MhfeWallet: identical Uint8Array values consisting of 0xff followed by the public marker text; byte equality passes preparation. Neither case runs drawing or Argon2. Retain the terminated VM solely for diagnostic inspection.
findings.expected: Wrap both already-owned Rust byte vectors in SecretText before either fallible text conversion. Refusal must wipe both binding-owned allocations while preserving caller-owned buffers.
findings.observed: The first text(...)? precedes SecretText::new(repeat). Refusal drops the unguarded repeat Vec unwiped. Marker-pattern occurrences in actual WASM memory: 10 in the direct case, 11 in the unchanged public class/actual worker-source case; reverse-input and reviewPassword controls: zero. Caller buffers survive; worker JS copies are wiped; worker is terminated. Counts are pattern occurrences, not counts of separate allocations.
findings.impact: Limited exceptional-path failure of best-effort owned-secret cleanup. Node VM instrumentation deliberately retains otherwise terminated memory; no access to a terminated real browser worker, persistence, swap exposure, key disclosure or exfiltration was demonstrated. JS cleanup cannot wipe wasm-bindgen's separately owned Rust vector.
findings.recommendedFix: Construct SecretText owners for both arguments before decoding either. Search other multi-secret bindings for the same ownership-before-fallibility invariant.
findings.requiredVerification: Run the retained malformed-first/public-identical probes and reverse/review controls with zero owned repeat-marker residuals; preserve caller bytes, JS wiping and termination. Add a production regression for this sequencing.

findings.title: Accepted maximum two-root search scopes overflow reported address count
findings.reproduction: Compile and run address-search-boundary.rs against the freshly built release libmhfe.rlib. SearchLimits::new(2147483648, 2147483648), public Bitcoin Cash legacy or Ethereum Classic address, AddressSearch::new(&address, None, limits), then read the description count. No key derivation, candidate search or KDF is executed.
findings.expected: Either report the exact aggregate or clearly refuse an unrepresentable aggregate after individually valid limits; never report an authoritative zero.
findings.observed: The u64 roots * 2 chains * accounts * indexes multiplication wraps 2^64 to zero for both two-root profiles. Expected 18446744073709551616, observed 0. The one-root maximum returns 9223372036854775808 correctly; the two adjacent two-root cases return 18446744065119617024 correctly. Debug source implies an overflow panic, but no debug runtime probe was run.
findings.impact: Incorrect native public API metadata at explicitly accepted extreme counts. Default and browser-produced scopes are smaller; no astronomical search, wrong derived key or secret disclosure was demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Use checked arithmetic with a clear aggregate-limit refusal, or an exact wider representation throughout the API. Do not silently saturate or redefine individual accepted limits without documentation.
findings.requiredVerification: Add metadata-only max/adjacent/invalid-count and explicit-path-one regressions for one-root and two-root profiles, in debug and release. Preserve all normal derivation vectors.

findings.title: Semicolon-free module declarations hide following active code from the clone gate
findings.reproduction: Run clone-controls.mjs: independently valid ESM ASI import and ASI re-export fixtures precede matching 126-token active function bodies. Compare the explicit-semicolon import control.
findings.expected: The declaration exclusion ends at the actual import/re-export boundary; following active code remains eligible regardless of valid semicolon style.
findings.observed: Both semicolon-free cases return no copies / exit 0; explicit-semicolon control detects the body / exit 1. The scanner advances until the next literal semicolon, swallowing active body tokens.
findings.impact: Limited assurance gap in the maintenance gate. The normal formatter inserts semicolons, reducing current practical exposure. No currently hidden production clone was established. This is distinct from AUD-012-ARC001's export-function/from classification root.
findings.recommendedFix: Recognize complete declaration boundaries with a suitable parser or a safe bounded tokenizer; do not skip through an unrelated body semicolon.
findings.requiredVerification: Keep independently parsed ASI import/re-export controls, semicolon control, exported functions/classes, dynamic import/import.meta and legitimate declaration exclusions.

findings.title: A string literal is accepted as a deliberate-copy comment waiver
findings.reproduction: Run clone-controls.mjs's noncomment-marker case: nearby const explanation = "deliberate copy"; precedes a matching 133-token block. The legitimate comment waiver is a separate passing control.
findings.expected: Only an actual documented comment with the required waiver marker/reason may suppress a clone, not ordinary executable string content.
findings.observed: Raw line matching recognizes the string as the waiver and returns exit 0 for the matching block. Ordinary unmarked positive control detects the same 133-token body.
findings.impact: Limited maintenance-gate false negative; no present production clone or security bypass was established.
findings.recommendedFix: Record lexical comment spans and apply waiver matching only to eligible comments, validating the intended documented reason.
findings.requiredVerification: Add ordinary strings, escaped/template strings and real-comment positive/negative controls; keep existing legitimate deliberate-copy behavior.

findings.title: A marked first occurrence suppresses comparisons between later unmarked clones
findings.reproduction: Run clone-controls.mjs: three equal 133-token blocks with A deliberately marked, B/C unmarked. Reverse enumeration so an unmarked block is first as the matched control.
findings.expected: Exempting A does not exempt the B/C pair; the result is independent of file enumeration order.
findings.observed: Every equal window is compared only with the first anchor. A-marked-first returns exit 0 because each pair includes A and is suppressed; unmarked-first detects the unmarked pair / exit 1.
findings.impact: Limited maintenance-gate false negative and enumeration-order sensitivity; no current hidden production copy was proved. Independent of the marker-not-comment root.
findings.recommendedFix: Exclude permitted occurrences before choosing an anchor, or choose an unmarked anchor so unmarked peers are still compared.
findings.requiredVerification: Add marked-first/middle/last, reordered multi-file and same-file groups, and legitimate marked-only controls without quadratic redundant reporting.

informationalRecommendations.title: Keep current owner boundaries
informationalRecommendations.detail: ContainerFacts/OriginalFacts/Encryption/Rekey/RecoveryStatus own rules; CLI/WASM delegate. Four browser classes compose shared runtime/one WASM. Private state and narrow engine/RNG/progress/host interfaces generally follow all ten principles. Do not wrap pure helpers in classes or split files by size. Cleanup gaps do not require broad redesign.

informationalRecommendations.title: Avoid repeated curve-point calculation
informationalRecommendations.detail: program_for computes a compressed key before branching; Taproot/Keccak compute the point again. Compute only the required representation or reuse the point. Parent-public-key reuse across child indexes is another profiling candidate. Preserve address vectors and secret wiping.

informationalRecommendations.title: Reduce candidate-check allocations
informationalRecommendations.detail: Inner Vec<Vec<u16>> could use fixed two-record/flat storage if profiling shows benefit. Benchmark enumeration/allocations/RSS, preserving order, cancellation and matches.

informationalRecommendations.title: Reuse parsed phrase owners conservatively
informationalRecommendations.detail: Some paths parse a phrase again. Internal parsed-owner reuse could help if measured, likely little versus Argon2. Avoid retained secrets, weakened locks or reordered refusals.

informationalRecommendations.title: Profile clone gate after correcting misses
informationalRecommendations.detail: Per-window slice/join string keys cost O(N*K). Rolling hash with exact collision checks is only warranted if profiling finds meaningful cost; fix correctness first.

informationalRecommendations.title: Delegate address-limit adjustment
informationalRecommendations.detail: Reference-owner operation may reduce reconstruction coupling if useful. No additional confirmed rule copy or mandatory module extraction found.

informationalRecommendations.title: Origin-bind rekey confirmation as explicit hardening
informationalRecommendations.type: optional API hardening, not a confirmed finding
informationalRecommendations.detail: Native callers can mix ConfirmedPhrase objects, but active CLI keeps the pair together and BrowserRekey owns its result. Caller affirmation is trusted; no supported-workflow corruption found. Replacement rehearsal intentionally belongs to caller workflow before destroying the old backup.

priorFindingVerification.scopedResult: Partially fixed, narrowly incomplete. Invalid 2**32 worker count refuses before copying, and six setup/partial-start controls wipe owned arrays, stop partial jobs and allow slot reuse. One bounded injected failure remains: new Uint8Array(0) after the first encoded copy but before try at web/wallet.js:148 leaves one owned copy unwiped.
priorFindingVerification.remainingFix: Create the empty repetition before copying the first secret or place every later constructor under cleanup using an optional owner. Retain all six passing controls and the initial-empty-array failure regression.
priorFindingVerification.limitations: Synthetic constructor refusal only; no actual OOM, browser memory access or disclosure. Retains the original finding ID because all-setup cleanup is the same root.

priorFindingVerification.scopedResult: RecoveredPhrase fields are private; read accessors and into_phrase() move/read the lock-owning value. Positive read/consume witness compiles. Original safe public-mutation witness is refused with two E0616 diagnostics. Native memory ownership/locking tests pass.
priorFindingVerification.limitations: Compile witnesses prove API ownership boundaries, not runtime recovery, swap exposure, guaranteed erasure or mathematical secrecy. DOC001 separately records stale example adaptation.

priorFindingVerification.scopedResult: The original exported-function containing from is examined and its 133-token copy detected; legitimate declaration exclusions and production self-test work. Verification is scoped to the original classification root; the new ASI-boundary issue has a different root.
priorFindingVerification.limitations: Does not imply correct complete ESM parsing or absence of other false negatives.

priorFindingVerification.scopedResult: NaN, Infinity, 0, -1, 1, 1.5 and an unsafe integer are refused with exit 2; production self-test passes; unknown/extra-argument refusal is also source-reviewed.
priorFindingVerification.limitations: Original threshold defect verified; unrelated tokenizer/waiver defects remain separately open.

executionSummary.doc: 3 passed, 1 failed; ordinary cargo test exit 101

assessment: Module/class direction and library delegation are sound; no broad extraction or extra classes required by confirmed evidence. Six new Low findings plus one narrowly incomplete continued Low AUD012 finding remain. Three other AUD012 findings verified in their original scopes. DOC001 blocks mandatory ordinary cargo-test gate, although it is a limited documentation defect. No Critical/High/Medium or key disclosure confirmed. No proof of complete erasure, zero duplication or cryptographic security. Optional optimizations unbenchmarked; no release acceptance.
limitations: No full-size Argon2 operations, ignored full-cost tests, complete suite-3/suite-4 or independent Python vector replay. Known-answer tests include up to 256 MiB; real-browser operations use the existing reduced 256 KiB/one-pass configuration, not altered production parameters.

No >13 GB workload and no full card generation. After the user memory constraint, runtime suites were sequential, monitored at 3 GiB aggregate RSS with a 2 GiB available-memory reserve and a 3 GiB startup minimum. Earlier ordinary Rust run predates monitoring; no measured-memory claim for that run.

RSS is sampled once per second, may double-count shared pages, is not a hard allocation cap, does not diagnose the interruption or control unrelated sessions. Highest guarded peak 1279123456 bytes (~1.19 GiB); lowest available memory 5204623360 bytes (~4.85 GiB); no guard termination.

No canonical Docker/fresh WASM rebuild, final archive/signature/reproducibility acceptance, paid CI, release publication or Windows/macOS runtime. Existing package stamps/source equality/freshness are not canonical reproducibility.
No external Deriver end-to-end fields/workflow/handover, desktop/mobile visual or host accessibility acceptance. Standalone package classes/harness pages are separate evidence.
No exhaustive upstream internals audit/current dependency advisory or literature search. First-party integration and pinned manifests/licenses were reviewed, without new network/install behavior.

WASM marker inspection deliberately retains terminated Node VM memory. It is not access to terminated real-browser workers, swap exposure, persistence, exfiltration or guaranteed OS erasure. Pattern counts are not counts of logical allocations.

Setup failures are bounded synthetic constructor/copy/start injections. Actual OOM or zero-length allocation exhaustion was not induced. Real browsers and other lifecycle controls are separate evidence.

RecoveredPhrase witnesses are compile-only. Address-count probe is metadata-only against fresh release rlib; debug overflow is source inference, not executed panic. No astronomical search or real wallet material.
Clone controls use virtual synthetic files/unchanged production algorithm and independently parse ESM. Misses are not evidence of a currently hidden production clone or proof of all semantic DRY.

Aborted pre-ultra preparation excluded. Fresh explicit-ultra review and the resume after the interruption use identical source bytes. Empty interrupted records, initial harness mistakes and restricted EPERM captures are preserved, not claimed as passes.

Coordinator GPT-6.1/ultra setting is user-reported; exact client model/service identifier and actual coordinator effort telemetry unavailable, so canonical values are null. Review agents explicitly assigned gpt-6.1-sol / ultra; collaboration is not independent specialist certification.

Source/spec comparisons and known answers are not mathematical cryptographic proof. The separate specification has dirty documents; closure reference hashes identify cited files, not a clean release or proof of cross-session stability.
Only audit report/index/follow-up/harness/local evidence edits. No production/test/fixture/dependency/vendor/workflow edits, repository copies/worktrees, commits, pushes, tags or releases.

designPrinciples.assessment: Operation/facts types own one cohesive concern; CLI reading/printing stays separate.
Suite/reference/check variants centralize behavior; no new scattered dispatch defect confirmed.
Native/browser Argon2 engines keep the shared callback/result contract; corresponding known answers pass.
Engine, RNG and progress interfaces are narrow; four browser classes expose their own module surface.
Engine/RNG/progress/host behavior is supplied through traits or small callbacks, rather than terminal-only library code.
Container/reference/length/password rules generally delegate to owners; documented early JS refusals have library/runtime parity checks. Lexical assurance defects are separately tracked.
RecoveredPhrase accessors now preserve the owned locked value; exceptional guard gaps remain in the SEC findings.
Browser classes use shared runtime/module/slot helpers and one WASM without a deep class hierarchy.
Different native/browser engines and supplied callbacks use shared contracts; no confirmed need for a new abstraction layer.
ContainerFacts, OriginalFacts, Encryption, Rekey and RecoveryStatus answer their own questions; no further mandatory module extraction confirmed.
